artifacts.summary: Root cause proven by live reproduction: cycle_plan_dispatch_hash()'s strip pattern in orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh never strips the Issue Log's [--dispatch-seq N] placeholder (added by commit 21f282089 on 2026-10-03), so genuinely identical dispatches never hash equal, the streak counter resets to 1 every cycle, and the halt's streak>=2 trigger is never satisfied. Trigger predicate, back-out block, and call site are all correct and unreached. Doc description is accurate; Group 28/29 fixtures are not stale. Recommends a one-line normalizer fix, a corrected comment, a back-pointer comment in the generating script, a new Group 27 regression case, and separately landing an orphaned, unrelated, uncommitted H1 fix already sitting in the same file.

memory_candidates.content: Cross-script content-hashing failure shape: a script (orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's cycle_plan_dispatch_hash) that normalizes/hashes content generated by a sibling script (orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh) silently goes stale when the generating script adds a new per-invocation-varying interpolation without anyone updating the normalizer's strip pattern. The generating script had no comment pointing back to the normalizer, so the addition (an Issue Log [--dispatch-seq N] placeholder) landed cleanly with its own passing tests while silently breaking the identical-dispatch convergence guard in a completely different script. General lesson: any normalizer that strips 'known-varying' lines before hashing another script's output should have a back-pointer comment in the GENERATING script, not just an enumeration comment in the normalizer.

When N observed symptoms of a guard mechanism all fail together (dispatch issued, no blocked row, no stderr notice, file not backed out, lock held, counters advancing), prefer looking for ONE upstream input the guard's trigger predicate consumes (e.g. a hash-equality or comparison value) rather than assuming N separate bugs in the back-out logic itself. In this case all 14 failing assertions and 7 symptom categories traced to a single stale normalizer regex one level above the trigger predicate.
